pulmonology.heading: When to see a pulmonologist
pulmonology.introduction: Breathing and sleep problems can show up in everyday ways.

concerns.title: Getting winded walking or climbing stairs
A cough that won't go away
Wheezing or noisy breathing
Frequently coughing up mucus
Waking up gasping or being told you snore
Feeling sleepy despite a full night's rest

sources.title: National Cancer Institute: Pulmonologist
sources.supports: General role of a pulmonologist in diagnosing and treating lung disease; the introduction does not establish practice-specific services.

sources.title: NHLBI: COPD Symptoms
sources.supports: Breathlessness with activity, ongoing cough, mucus, and wheezing; these experiences do not establish COPD.

sources.title: American Lung Association: Warning Signs of Lung Disease
sources.supports: Persistent cough, breathlessness, ongoing mucus, and noisy breathing can warrant evaluation and have multiple possible causes.

sources.title: NHLBI: Sleep Apnea Symptoms
sources.supports: Loud snoring, observed breathing pauses, gasping during sleep, and daytime sleepiness; select sleep entries only for practices with verified relevant services.

psychotherapy.heading: What brings you here?
psychotherapy.introduction: You may recognize some of these experiences in your own life.

concerns.title: Worry that is hard to quiet
The same relationship conflicts keep returning
Being hard on yourself
Finding your way after a loss
A life change leaves you unsure what comes next
Illness has changed how you feel about yourself

sources.title: NIMH: Psychotherapies
sources.supports: Reasons to seek therapy, daily functioning, and general description of psychotherapy.

psychiatry.heading: Does any of this feel familiar?
psychiatry.introduction: You may know what feels difficult without knowing why.

concerns.title: Feeling low or losing interest in things you enjoyed
Worry or panic takes over
Struggling to focus, remember tasks, or get started
You can't get the rest you need
Your mood and energy feel unpredictable
You've tried care, but still feel stuck
Unwanted thoughts or repeated checking feel hard to stop
Hearing or seeing things others don't

sources.title: NIMH: My Mental Health: Do I Need Help?
sources.supports: Recognizable changes in mood, interest, concentration, sleep, energy, and daily functioning.

sources.title: American Psychiatric Association: What is Psychiatry?
sources.supports: Psychiatric evaluation and general range of treatments.

sources.title: NIMH: Psychotherapies
sources.supports: Discussing ongoing difficulties and considering other care approaches.

sources.title: NIMH: Bipolar Disorder
sources.supports: Changes in mood, energy, and sleep; concern wording does not establish a diagnosis.

sources.title: NIMH: Panic Disorder: What You Need to Know
sources.supports: Sudden episodes of intense fear or discomfort described in everyday language as waves of panic.

sources.title: NIMH: Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
sources.supports: Recurring thoughts and repetitive behaviors that interfere with daily life.

sources.title: NIMH: Understanding Psychosis
sources.supports: Hearing or seeing things others do not; these experiences can have multiple causes and require assessment.
